target:
abbrev Def1 := Set ArithmeticSentence

def Def5 (K : Def1) (F : ArithmeticTheory) : Prop := K = F.theory

def Def6 (K : Def1) : Prop := ∃ F : ArithmeticTheory, F.RE ∧ Def5 K F
a_raw: {"translation":"Def1 is an abbreviation for the type of sets of closed arithmetic sentences; it imposes no condition on those sets. For a set K of such sentences and an arithmetic axiom set F, Def5(K, F) means that K is exactly the set of theorems of F: for every arithmetic sentence σ, σ belongs to K if and only if σ is derivable from F. For a given K, Def6(K) means that there exists an arithmetic axiom set F such that F is recursively enumerable and Def5(K, F) holds for that same F. The recursive enumerability condition is on F as an axiom set. F need not equal K or be closed under deduction; it is the full theorem set of F that must equal K. No consistency or truth-in-the-standard-model hypothesis is imposed."}
translation: Def1 is an abbreviation for the type of sets of closed arithmetic sentences; it imposes no condition on those sets. For a set K of such sentences and an arithmetic axiom set F, Def5(K, F) means that K is exactly the set of theorems of F: for every arithmetic sentence σ, σ belongs to K if and only if σ is derivable from F. For a given K, Def6(K) means that there exists an arithmetic axiom set F such that F is recursively enumerable and Def5(K, F) holds for that same F. The recursive enumerability condition is on F as an axiom set. F need not equal K or be closed under deduction; it is the full theorem set of F that must equal K. No consistency or truth-in-the-standard-model hypothesis is imposed.

divergences.description: Def1 fixes the language to first-order arithmetic, whereas the excerpts speak of “sentences” without specifying a language. A parameter K of this type represents the mind’s outputs.

Def6 quantifies over a recursively enumerable axiom set F rather than a numerical index e. Koellner’s F_e corresponds to Lean’s F.theory, not to F itself. Since every recursively enumerable axiom set has an index, this changes the presentation but not the existential claim.

judgement.summary: Def5 expresses exact equality with the theorem set, leaving effectiveness separate. Def6 requires effectiveness of the same witness F, so it captures WMT as equality of outputs without adding a knowledge requirement.
